text:
marta: FYI customer acme-prod hit a big throughput drop on their dedicated pool (us-east-1). Latency jumped ~70ms -> 600ms and a smattering of 503s. Can we triage quickly?

sam: on it. any alert IDs or traces?

marta: alert: autoscale:pool-us-east-1-acme #34892 triggered twice in last 15m. attaching quick metric snapshot:
```
qps: 180 -> 420
avg latency: 72ms -> 610ms
95p latency: 120ms -> 1.1s
avg batch size: 1.2 tokens (down from 6.4)
avg tokens per request: 3
error rate: 0.4% -> 2.6% (503/504)
```

jordan: that avg batch size is suspicious — looks like heavy tiny-req traffic creating lots of micro-batches. could be a noisy tenant packing problem.

ejane: (joining) do we have batcher logs?

marta: pasted a relevant log tail: 
```
2026-03-17T15:02:11Z batcher[pool-acme]: accept req id=abcd123 small=true tokens=2 wait_ms=1
2026-03-17T15:02:11Z batcher[pool-acme]: schedule batch id=xx size=2 max_batch_tokens=2048 window_ms=8
2026-03-17T15:02:12Z scheduler[pool-acme]: dispatch batch id=xx -> worker-9
2026-03-17T15:02:12Z worker-9: inference start tokens=2 kv_hits=0
2026-03-17T15:02:12Z worker-9: inference end duration=590ms queue_wait=540ms
2026-03-17T15:02:12Z autoscaler[pool-acme]: replicas=3 -> 3 (min_replicas=3, cpu=78%)
```

sam: queue_wait 540ms is the killer. dispatcher is starving for larger batches so it dispatches quickly but workers spend long time per micro request (context switching/overhead).

jordan: also see autoscaler didn't scale because min_replicas locked at 3. cluster can't buy throughput by adding replicas because each worker still gets tiny batches => poor throughput.

elainE: quick mitigations: (1) temporarily increase max_batch_wait/window_ms to give batcher ~20ms to accumulate, (2) bump min_replicas to 5 for this pool, (3) throttle the noisy tenant routing if we can identify it.

marta: can we identify the tenant? we have tenant headers in logs. snippet: 
```
req id=abcd123 tenant=acme-ui user=svc-frontend tokens=2
req id=efgh456 tenant=widget-labs user=svc-batch tokens=128
```

ajordan: looks like acme-ui is the noisy one — many tiny UI calls. request pattern: 200 rps of 1-3 token calls. Repro locally w/ a load script: 
```bash
# hits /v1/generate with tiny prompt repeatedly
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":1}' &
  sleep 0.005
done
```

# or python async worker that does many short requests concurrently
```python
# minimal repro: many concurrent tiny requests
import asyncio, aiohttp
async def r(i):
  async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
    await s.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', json={'prompt':'x','max_tokens':1}, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer TOKEN'})
async def main():
  await asyncio.gather(*[r(i) for i in range(1000)])
```

sam: thanks. Action plan:
- I'll open a support ticket and tell acme to pause UI rapid polling (support-bot will send templated mitigation).
- ops: temporarily set pool-us-east-1-acme min_replicas=5 and batch_window_ms=20 (from 8).
- eng-runtime: follow-up on longer-term scheduler improvements to prefer packing by tokens instead of immediate dispatch on small batch counts.

ops-bot: runbook step executed: set min_replicas=5 for pool-us-east-1-acme (done), set batch_window_ms=20 (done). Monitoring for next 10m.

marta: after changes, quick metric diff: 
```
avg batch size: 4.9 tokens (from 1.2)
avg latency: 78ms
95p: 210ms
error rate: 0.6%
```

jordan: much better. still a bit higher than baseline but acceptable. Long-term follow-ups: implement tenant-aware packing (prefer coalescing tiny requests from multiple tenants into single batch when privacy constraints allow), and autoscaler heuristics that consider effective throughput not just CPU.

elainE: I'll file runtime RFC for packing heuristics and a canary to shift batch_window per-tenant dynamically.

sam: I filed support ticket #ACME-527, emailed customer with temporary mitigation and ETA for deeper fix.

marta: marking this thread resolved for now. please add postmortem if similar regressions happen again. :thumbsup:
